questions.q: While editing a formula, pressing F4 on the reference A1 changes it to:
questions.solution: F4 cycles the reference through A1 -> $A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 -> A1. The first press makes it fully absolute.
questions.shortcut: One tap of F4 = full lock ($ before both letter and number).

questions.q: In the URL https://www.ssc.gov.in, the component '.in' is the:
questions.solution: .in is the country-code top-level domain for India. 'https' is the protocol, 'www' the sub-domain/host, 'ssc' the registered domain name.
questions.shortcut: Read right to left: .in = TLD, .gov = second level, ssc = the name.

questions.q: How many links are needed for a full mesh topology with 5 computers?
questions.shortcut: Five nodes -> 5x4/2; the 20 option is the un-halved trap for those using n(n-1) with n=5... actually 20 = n x (n-1), another halving slip - always divide by 2.

questions.q: In Windows File Explorer, which shortcut creates a new folder in the current location?
questions.solution: Ctrl+Shift+N creates a new folder in Explorer. Plain Ctrl+N opens a new Explorer window. In Chrome, Ctrl+Shift+N opens an incognito window.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl+N = new window; add Shift for a new folder.

questions.q:
Select the correct question tag.

Nobody called while I was out, ___
questions.solution: *Nobody* makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; indefinite pronouns for people (*nobody, everyone, someone*) are picked up by **they**. The simple past *called* takes *did* → **did they?**
questions.shortcut: Negative word → positive tag; nobody → they.

questions.q:
Choose the correct order of the parts to make a meaningful sentence.

**1.** Manual work is steadily giving way to machines. **P:** This has led to unemployment in some sectors. **Q:** But new jobs have appeared in technology. **R:** Workers must therefore learn new skills. **S:** Machines work faster and never tire. **6.** Adaptability is the only security left.
questions.solution: **S** explains S1 (why machines replace work) → **P** ('This has led to') draws the unemployment consequence → **Q** ('But') contrasts with new jobs → **R** ('therefore') concludes. SPQR.
questions.shortcut: Cause-effect pair S→P; contrast Q; therefore-conclusion R.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The children / were playing / in a garden / near an university.
questions.solution: *University* begins with the consonant sound *yu*, so it takes **a**: 'near a university'. The article follows sound, not spelling.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Each of the boys / have submitted / his assignment / well before the deadline.
questions.solution: *Each* is invariably singular: 'Each of the boys **has** submitted'. Note that part 3 (*his*) is correct — a singular pronoun after *each* is exactly what standard grammar wants.
questions.shortcut: 'Each of ___' → singular verb, even though the nearest noun is plural.

questions.q: The capital of the **Satavahana** kingdom was —
questions.solution: The Satavahanas ruled from **Pratishthana (Paithan)** on the Godavari (Maharashtra). Vatapi = Chalukyas of Badami; Manyakheta = Rashtrakutas; Kanchipuram = Pallavas.

questions.q: Which country topped the medal table at the Commonwealth Games 2026?
questions.solution: Australia topped the table for the third consecutive Games with 70 gold and 171 total medals.
questions.shortcut: Australia has topped every CWG medal table since 2006 except Birmingham 2022's tie context — default answer.

questions.q: The Durand Line forms the boundary between:
questions.solution: The **Durand Line** (1893, drawn by Sir Mortimer Durand) marks the **Pakistan–Afghanistan** border. India–China is the McMahon Line and India–Pakistan is the Radcliffe Line.

questions.q: Who discovered the neutron?
questions.solution: **James Chadwick** discovered the neutron in **1932** (Nobel Prize 1935). Thomson discovered the electron and Rutherford the atomic nucleus.
questions.shortcut: 'Tom Ran Chasing' — the third particle goes to Chadwick.

questions.q: In what ratio must rice at ₹36 per kg be mixed with rice at ₹24 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹30 per kg?
If $x = 3 + 2\sqrt{2}$, then the value of $\sqrt{x} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$ is:
What are the last two digits of $7^{2008}$?
Two numbers, when divided by 17, leave remainders 13 and 11 respectively. What is the remainder when their product is divided by 17?
questions.solution: Product of remainders $= 13 \times 11 = 143 = 17 \times 8 + 7$. Remainder **7**.

questions.q: **Kiran starts facing East and walks 5 km, turns right and walks 3 km, turns right and walks 5 km, then turns right again and walks 2 km.** In which direction is she from the starting point?
questions.solution: East 5 → (5, 0); right → South 3 → (5, −3); right → West 5 → (0, −3); right → North 2 → (0, −1). The x-components cancel; 1 km of Southward drift remains → **South** of the start.
questions.shortcut: Cancel East-West first (5 and 5); the leftover South 1 km decides the direction.
questions.pattern: direction of the endpoint from start

questions.q: Pointing to Deepa, Ramesh said, **"She is the daughter of my father's sister."** How is Deepa related to Ramesh?
questions.solution: My father's sister = Ramesh's aunt; her daughter = Ramesh's **cousin**. (Niece is the reverse — the child of one's own sibling.)
questions.shortcut: Aunt's children are cousins; sibling's children are nephews/nieces.

questions.q: Eight friends **A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit in a row facing north. A sits second to the left of E. E sits third to the left of D. G and D sit at the two extreme ends. C is an immediate neighbour of A (on A's left). B sits immediately to the right of E, and F immediately to the right of B.** Who sits **third from the right end**?
questions.solution: Ends: G and D. D must leave three seats to its left for E, so D = seat 8, G = seat 1. E = D − 3 = seat 5; A = seat 3; C on A's left = seat 2; B = seat 6, F = seat 7. Remaining H takes seat 4. Third from the right = seat 6 = **B**.
questions.shortcut: 'Third to the left of an end' forces which end is which — start there and chain inward.
